title: Direct Bus Services to Geylang Serai Market before Hari Raya Puasa and Hari Raya Haji
what_it_is: Direct Bus Services to Geylang Serai Market before Hari Raya Puasa and Hari Raya Haji

sections.label: Direct bus services to Geylang Serai
sections.summary: MP asks if LTA will plan two direct bus services to Geylang Serai market before Hari Raya Puasa and Hari Raya Haji from Bedok areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked 	the Minister for Transport whether LTA will consider planning for two direct bus services to the Geylang Serai market in the month before Hari Raya Puasa and Hari Raya Haji from main roads around Bedok South, Bedok Central and Bedok North.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: They include Services 7, 26 and 30 from Bedok Interchange in Bedok Central, 28 and 67 from Bedok North Avenue 3, and 2, 24, 28 and 67 from New Upper Changi Road which serves Bedok South.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: From previous years' experience, these bus services are sufficient to cater to the festive crowds.

sections.label: Bus waiting times complaints
sections.summary: Recorded complaints show bus service 229 waiting time up to 16 minutes, and transfers to services 2 or 28 up to 19 or 15 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Some of the complaints that we have recorded show us that, say, for example, bus service 229, the waiting time could take up to 16 minutes, and, for example, if you take bus service 229 and you transfer to bus service 2 or 28, bus service 2 takes up to 19 minutes' waiting time, bus service 28 can be up to 15 minutes.

sections.label: Ridership and direct services demand
sections.summary: Services from mature towns to Chinatown have low ridership of 150 to 200 riders daily, so LTA would consider added services only if demand is sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This includes charging higher fares, but it is still centred upon ridership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: And even these services from different mature towns to Chinatown have low ridership of 150 to 200 riders per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: It comes back to my point in the earlier answer – whether the added services would be considered would depend on the demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Should there be sufficient demand, LTA would certainly consider such services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But at the moment, with the surveys, there is not enough ridership to justify direct services.
